L2-normalized temporal means provide a direction, not confidence. For unit item vectors, m=Σwᵢxᵢ/Σwᵢ has resultant length R=||m|| measuring directional concentration; normalizing m discards R ([SciPy](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.directional_stats.html)). Consequently, a singleton produces a full-strength direction, while an incoherent history can produce an equally strong residual whenever ||m|| exceeds epsilon. Cancellation can reflect multiple legitimate interests, not noise. Relevant alternatives explicitly model uncertainty—[STOSA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06035) uses Gaussian covariance—or address irrelevant interactions, as discussed in [Denoising Self-attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04120). Neither establishes normalized pooling alone as consensus detection.

Self-inclusion creates an algebraic agreement bias: for S=Σwⱼxⱼ, xᵢᵀS=wᵢ+Σⱼ≠ᵢwⱼxᵢᵀxⱼ. Thus a singleton agrees perfectly with its own pooled direction; n equally weighted orthogonal items each have cosine 1/√n despite zero pairwise agreement. These are direct derivations. Use a strictly preceding-history pool or leave-one-out agreement, with an explicit no-evidence branch. A proposed evidence-sensitive residual is g·normalize(m), where g depends on R and effective sample size n_eff=(Σw)²/Σw², and vanishes without independent support. This is a design proposal requiring validation; embedding agreement cannot establish unobserved conformity traits.

[PyTorch normalize](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.normalize.html) computes m/max(||m||,ε). Differentiating gives Jacobian (I−uuᵀ)/||m|| above ε and I/ε below ε, away from the boundary. Zero input therefore returns zero but can have large gradients; epsilon prevents division by zero, not instability. Pool in float32, mask padding, and consider a smooth residual m/(||m||+τ), τ>0, plus an evidence gate.
